Appliance Display Wall

COLMO Refrigerator Display Wall

A refrigerator is a large product. If it is simply placed against a wall, customers see its size before they feel its value.

For COLMO, REYI built each model into a composed architectural frame. Warm light, dark textured panels and fine metal lines turn a row of appliances into a calm, complete kitchen scene—helping customers imagine not only the refrigerator, but the life around it.

Product View

From a row of appliances to a complete kitchen scene

Each refrigerator has its own bay, yet the full wall reads as one continuous composition. The dark background visually reduces the bulk of the appliances; warm vertical lighting defines each model without turning the wall into a bright sales shelf. Customers can compare products clearly while remaining inside the same refined brand atmosphere.

How the Experience Is Built

Four details shape how the products are perceived

A Clear Brand Anchor

The illuminated COLMO logo sits above the full composition, so the wall is recognized as one branded destination before individual models are compared.

Model-specific Bays

Every opening is planned around the real width and depth of its appliance, keeping gaps and front alignment visually controlled.

Warm Vertical Light

Light follows the sides of each bay, separating dark appliance forms gently and making surface finishes easier to read.

Repeatable Construction

The visual language can be translated into store-specific modules while preserving the same proportions, finishes and brand recognition across locations.

Material & Lighting Details

The premium feeling is carried by small, controlled details

Warm linear light meets the dark textured surface and fine metal edge, adding depth without distracting from the appliance.

The illuminated logo is integrated into the header rather than added as a separate sign, keeping the brand expression quiet and assured.

Bay depth, front alignment and edge finishing are coordinated around the real product, so different models still belong to one visual system.
